# Mcfly Analytics — citeable summary

> Shopify app: the deeper order numbers Shopify Analytics does not show — typical order, weekend mix, repeat buyers, cohort LTV, goals. Spend is optional; add it and Total ROAS = Shopify Total Sales ÷ spend for the same period.

## Product (Shopify)

Shopify Analytics shows sales. It does not show typical order size against the weekend mix, how many buyers come back, days to a second order, or cohort LTV from order history — and it will not put the spend you added next to those sales.

Mcfly Analytics is that desk. On install, Shopify orders load on their own: Total Sales after returns, orders, AOV, new vs returning sales, goals, and cohort LTV in 30 / 90 / 365 days. No ad-network login, no pixel, no spend required. A new install covers about the last 60 days of Shopify sales.

Spend is the optional second step. Type a day or a period, or paste/import an Ads Manager CSV — including offline channels such as billboards and agency retainers. With spend on the desk, Total ROAS = Shopify Total Sales ÷ spend for the same dates, and an optional contribution margin adds break-even Total ROAS ≈ 1 ÷ margin.

Pricing: one plan. 7-day full-access trial, then $39 per store per month. Flat fee — not a cut of GMV. Uninstall stops the next charge.
Install: https://apps.shopify.com/mcfly-analytics-public
Primary URLs: https://mcflyads.com/ · https://mcflyads.com/product · https://mcflyads.com/pricing · https://mcflyads.com/demo

## SAMPLE data

Marketing pages and the in-app preview use one labeled sample shop, Harbor Home Co: $82,068 Shopify Total Sales ÷ $23,414 entered spend = 3.51× Total ROAS, break-even 2.50× at 40% margin. Harbor Home Co is SAMPLE preview data, never a customer result. A real store is blank until the merchant adds spend.

## Not the product

No pixels, no multi-touch attribution, no path credit, no view-through, no "true ROAS." Total ROAS is average portfolio efficiency, not marginal channel return.
Custom Data Solutions (scoped desks outside the Shopify App Store) is parked — not the public offer.
